m:castle: Adult ticket £23.50 (about €28) bought online, £26 (about €31) on the day, with a time slot: from the official website, read on 13 October 2026. From 1 October to 31 March the castle opens at 9:30am, last entry is at 4pm and it closes at 5pm (April to September it usually closes at 6pm: to be confirmed); closed on 25 and 26 December, on 24 December it closes at 4pm. The «One o'Clock Gun» fires every day at 1pm except Sunday. The castle may close in bad weather: check edinburghcastle.scot the day before. Online tickets often sell out: book ahead.
m:royalmile: Free to walk around. St Giles is free to enter, with a suggested donation (a small ticket for the clock tower climb, about £6): hours read on a secondary listing, Monday–Friday 10am–6pm, Saturday 9am–5pm, Sunday 1–5pm, to be confirmed on stgilescathedral.org.uk. Along the middle of the Royal Mile the places are aimed at tourists: the genuine ones are in the closes.
m:holyrood: Adult ticket £22 (about €26) in advance, £26 (about €31) on the day, from the official website (rct.uk). From October to December 2026 the palace is only open Thursday to Monday (closed Tuesday and Wednesday): until 31 October 9:30am–6pm (last entry 4:30pm), from 1 November 9:30am–4:30pm (last entry 3:15pm); closed on 25 and 26 December. Hours read in an official document from November 2025, so to be confirmed on rct.uk before you go. The palace closes when the King or the royal family use it.
m:arthur: The park is open all year and entry is free. Allow 1 and a half to 2 hours up and down. The wind at the top is almost always strong: bring a jacket and shoes with good grip, as the path gets slippery in the rain. In bad weather or poor light it's better to skip it.
m:nms: Free entry to the permanent collections. Open every day from 10am to 5pm; closed on 25 December (opens at noon on 26 December and 1 January). Some temporary exhibitions are paid. From the official website nms.ac.uk, read on 13 October 2026. Allow at least 2 hours: there are many galleries.
m:calton: The hill is open at all hours and free; the climb from Waterloo Place takes 5–10 minutes on foot. The Nelson Monument (143 steps) is open every day from 10am to 3:30pm and costs £7.50 (about €9): hours and price from a secondary website, to be confirmed. The wind is strong and the steps are slippery in the rain.
m:princes: The gardens are free and open during the day. The Scott Monument has 287 narrow steps, costs about £8 (about €9.50) and is open roughly 10am–4pm in winter: data from a 2026 online guide, to be confirmed. In the colder months the gardens host the Christmas market: check the dates.
m:gallery: Free entry to the permanent collection. Typical hours are 10am to 5pm every day, but I couldn't read them on the official website: to be confirmed on nationalgalleries.org before you go.
m:grass: Free to walk around. Greyfriars Kirkyard is open during the day and free; the Grassmarket market is usually on Saturdays (to be confirmed). On rainy days the cobbled streets are slippery.
m:dean: The path and the village are free and always open. The Stockbridge market is usually on Sundays (to be confirmed). The waterside route is flat but can be muddy.
vd:larder: A local-produce Scottish café in a close a short walk from the Royal Mile: breakfasts with eggs and bacon, porridge, soups and sandwiches with local ingredients. The kind of place where locals go for lunch.
vp:larder: Breakfast or lunch is around £9–14 (about €11–17), menu not seen. Hours and prices from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:clarinda: An old-fashioned tea room on the Canongate, halfway between the castle and Holyrood Palace: Scottish breakfasts, scones with cream and jam, and tea in china cups.
vp:clarinda: Tea with a scone is around £6–9 (about €7–11); a full breakfast £9–13 (€11–15); menu not seen. Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:mums: A casual place near Greyfriars with Scottish home cooking: sausages and mash, meatloaf, meat pies, haggis and porridge at breakfast. Generous portions at fair prices.
vp:mums: A plate of sausages and mash is around £12–16 (about €14–19), menu not seen. Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:oink: A hatch on Victoria Street that has been serving rolls with freshly carved roast pork, stuffing and apple sauce for years: the typical quick lunch, eaten in the street.
vp:oink: A roll costs around £6–8 (about €7–9.50), menu not seen. Hours from guides, to be confirmed: it closes when the meat runs out.
vd:dogs: A modern Scottish restaurant on one of the most elegant streets of the New Town: seasonal meat and fish, often from small producers, at lower prices than the nearby places on George Street.
vp:dogs: A dinner with a main and a dessert is around £25–35 (about €30–40), menu not seen. Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:caferoyal: An 1863 Victorian pub with ceramic tiles and stained glass: the Oyster Bar serves oysters and fish, the Circle Bar fish and chips and Scottish beers. In the heart of the New Town, a minute from St Andrew Square.
vp:caferoyal: Fish and chips or a pie with a beer is around £15–22 (about €18–26), menu not seen. Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:tingthai: Thai street food near the university and the National Museum: rice noodles, curries and dishes to share, with good value for money.
vp:tingthai: A dish is around £11–15 (about €13–18), menu not seen. Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:pantry: A breakfast and brunch café in Stockbridge, famous for porridge, eggs with Scottish smoked salmon and homemade bread. A residential-neighbourhood spot, a quarter of an hour from Dean Village.
vp:pantry: Breakfast or brunch around £10–15 (about €12–18), menu not seen. Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:hectors: A Stockbridge pub with outdoor tables and simple Scottish food: pies, fish and chips, burgers and draught beers. Popular with locals.
vp:hectors: A dish is around £13–18 (about €15–21), menu not seen. Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:marys: A neighbourhood ice cream shop in the Grassmarket, with homemade ice cream in Scottish flavours (shortbread, toffee, tea), thick hot chocolate and small treats. For a sweet break after the castle.
vp:marys: An ice cream or a hot chocolate is around £4–6 (about €5–7), menu not seen. Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
cd:scott: 287 steps to the top of the Walter Scott monument, with views over Princes Street.
cn:camera: Camera Obscura and World of Illusions
cd:camera: Five floors of optical illusions and a camera obscura with a view of the city.
cd:marykings: The buried closes under the Royal Mile, visited with a costumed guide.
cd:britannia: Queen Elizabeth II's former royal yacht, in Leith.
cx:britannia: It's in Leith, about 4 km from the centre.
cd:zooedi: The zoo with pandas on the slope of Corstorphine Hill.
cd:whisky: A barrel ride through the Scotch whisky regions, with a tasting.
cd:dynamicearth: The story of the Earth, with an immersive experience at the foot of Arthur's Seat.
cd:botanico: Tropical glasshouses and the Chinese Garden, in one of the finest gardens in the UK.
cd:surgeons: The museum of surgery, with the story of Burke and Hare.
cd:georgian: A 1796 house with period furnishings on Charlotte Square.
